subject: Post-call: PII access logs sample & retention clarifications
thread_text:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finlytics.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: PII access logs sample & retention clarifications

Alex — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the data handling items you raised: 

1) What you need from us (priority): a small sample export of audit/log data showing who accessed PII (user-id, role), what action was performed (read/export/delete), resource identifier, timestamp, and whether the payload contained PII fields.
2) Export formats: you asked for both CSV and JSON examples and a description of our export pipeline (how we generate these extracts).
3) Retention & redaction: clarify default retention for access logs vs. payload retention, and what our configurable options are for shorter retention windows or hashing of identifiers.
4) Data residency: confirm whether audit logs and exports can be served from a US-only region for your legal team.
5) Evidence: your SOC/Procurement team will want an example extract plus a short schema doc and a pointer to the live retention/config UI or API.

Next steps I propose: 
- I’ll loop in Karthik (security) to prepare a redacted sample export and schema doc.
- Marissa will add the HubSpot deal link and help coordinate an NDA/PO if we need to speed up an evidence package.
- Alex, can you confirm the specific fields you want in the sample (e.g., full user email vs. hashed id) and whether you want a one-off export or an ongoing log-delivery arrangement?

I’ve attached the meeting minutes (stub) and our standard evidence checklist for quick reference.

Attachments: meeting_notes_postcall.txt (stub), evidence_checklist.pdf (stub)

—

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finlytics.io>

Cc: SaaSOps Security <security@saaops.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 15:03:12 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call: PII access logs sample & retention clarifications

Thanks Rishi — helpful recap. A couple clarifications from our side before the sample: 

- For compliance we'll need a CSV with these columns: timestamp (ISO8601 UTC), actor_type (human/service), actor_identifier (email or hashed id), action (read, write, export, delete), resource_type, resource_id, was_pii (true/false), pii_fields_mask (comma-separated list of field names that contained PII), request_id.
- Please include at least one example of an export action where the payload contained PII (fields masked), and one example of a read-by-a-service (e.g., background job) to show separation of actor_type.
- Retention: our legal team prefers access logs retained for 24 months but some product teams want 90 days. Please call out any policy guards for auto-deletion and how a customer can change retention.
- Residency: we need confirmation the logs and exports can be kept (and exported from) the US region only — that is a hard requirement.

If you can provide a single redacted CSV + JSON variant and a short schema doc we can share with our procurement team. If possible we’d like the sample by EOD Monday (6/15).

Cheers,
Alex Turner
Director, Security & Compliance
FinLytics

Alex / Rishi — attaching a redacted sample export and the extract schema. Notes below.

Attachments: finlytics_sample_kv_log.csv (redacted sample, 12 rows), redwood-audit-extract-schema.pdf (schema + field descriptions)

Quick notes on the sample and policy: 
- Format: CSV and a JSON-serializable line-per-event are generated by the same export endpoint. We included the CSV per your request; the JSON lines variant is identical in fields and can be produced on request.
- Fields included: timestamp_utc, actor_type, actor_id_hash, actor_email_masked, action, resource_type, resource_id, was_pii, pii_fields_mask, request_id, region. We default to hashing actor_id for exports; we can include the full email if the customer explicitly requests and has lawful basis (we document that in the audit).
- Retention windows: system access logs (event metadata) default to 24 months; payload-level storage (payloads that contain user content) default is 90 days. Both are configurable in Redwood Private/Dedicated via policy (API + Console). For Hosted customers we offer a managed retention override for enterprise contracts — changes require a signed request/PO to ensure we maintain compliance controls.
- Residency: audit logs are stored in the region where the tenant is provisioned. For US-only tenancy we can configure both storage and export endpoints to US regions; exports will not leave the region unless the customer enables cross-region replication.
- Access controls & evidence: we include per-event actor_id_hash and map logs to IAM principals; full access records are retained in the system and can be exported as CSV/JSON/Parquet. We can produce a certified extract (time-stamped and signed) for procurement/legal review if required.

Action items:
- Alex: confirm whether you want actor_email in clear or acceptable to receive actor_id_hash + masked email (we can include a reversible token if needed for investigations).
- Rishi / Marissa: I uploaded the sample and schema to the drive (link below) and will prepare a short one-page note for procurement describing what changes require an SLA/PO.
